summary: The author evaluates Claude Opus 5.5 and Sol 6.1 on generating an interactive 20,000-particle real-time water simulation, showing Opus 5.5's iSPH implementation alongside Sol's PBF approach.
summaryEn: Interactive 20,000 Water Particle Fluid Simulation Comparison

post.originalText:
I gave Sol 6.1 and Opus 5.5 the same test/prompt. 20,000 water particles, 60 fps

Sol 6.1 took the easy way...a hybrid method, PBF with a grid doing the heavy pressure math. Fast. 27/30. 60 fps

Opus 5.5 took the hard way, a pure iSPH method... particles work out pressure with each other. 28/30, but 10 fps in splashes (video sped up). Very slow output, rewrote its work from ground up a couple of times.

I respect the hard way but fair is fair. Sol's works.
